steps.text: Preheat the oven to 300 degrees F (150 degrees C).
Combine 3 tablespoons white sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl and set aside.
Blend brown sugar and 1/2 cup white sugar in a large bowl with a mixer on medium speed. Add butter and blend until grainy. Add eggs and vanilla, mixing until light and fluffy.
Whisk flour, baking soda, and salt together in a separate bowl.
Add to butter-sugar mixture, mixing at low speed just long enough to combine. Overmixing makes tough cookies.
Roll dough into 1-inch balls, then roll each ball into cinnamon sugar to coat. Place cookies on ungreased cookie sheets
Bake in the preheated oven for 18 to 20 minutes. Remove from sheets and let cool on racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Cinnamon Sugar Butter Cookies
raw_recipe.description: This recipe for cinnamon sugar cookies is meant to taste like the favorite Mrs. Fields' cookies — for those times when you want to make them at home.

review.reviewBody: I feel compelled to review this because it represents the beauty of allrecipes! I needed a cinnamon cookie recipe, found this one, read the rave reviews and gave it a shot. This is a very delicious cookie. I followed the instructions exactly (and I did also chill the dough as others did for at least 30 minutes) and they turned out perfectly. I used a tablespoon to measure out each cookie and the recipe made exactly one less of 4 dozen cookies! The cinnamon/sugar mixture was just right - not too cinnamon-y and enough to cover all the cookies. I see some have experienced dough too difficult to form into cookies - the key is to not have the butter TOO soft when mixing and definitely chilling before forming. The idea others have had to cut the cinnamon and instead add M&Ms is interesting. The difference is this butter cookie recipe has more brown sugar than white sugar which results in a more molasses-tasting cookie and I think chewier too, just FYI. Overall, I would highly recommend this! I'm not a huge fan of cinnamon and I love it.

Absolutely fabulous! I follow the recipe exactly, except for the vanilla. I always add twice the amount of vanilla. So delicious! Over beating really does ruin this cookie so make sure so be careful when mixing! Over all, one of my favorites!

These cookies were fantastic. So moist and chewy...even after 2 days. I added raisins but other than that I didnt change a thing! Think I am going to make some tonight for my girlfriends!***made these cookies again for a second time. This time, i used whole wheat flour instead of all purpose flour, 1/4 t. of baking powder to make them rise more, added a few shakes of nutmeg to the dry mix before adding it to the wet ingredients, and baked them in a 375 degree oven for 11 minutes. I also added the raisins again. They came out even better the 2nd time!!!!

These cookies are delicious! Similar to a snickerdoodle, but better being brown sugar is in the dough also, not just white sugar. I followed the recipe as written, but refrigerated the dough 30 minutes prior to rolling in balls. The dough is a bit sticky, do not add more flour just refrigerate it awhile. It's much easier to roll all the balls, then roll in the sugar cinnamon mixture, and set aside. I baked these for 18 minutes and they were perfectly crisp on the outside with a chewy, buttery center. I love cinnamon and cannot believe it took me this long to stumble across this recipe. I also made little sandwiches by filling some with vanilla frosting, which is wonderful. They are super delicious as is though. I have to remember to add these to my "favorite" list of cookies for the holidays, they are fabulous! Thanks for sharing this easy, yet wonderful recipe :)

These cookies are wonderful! Made a few changes based on personal preference. I baked them at 350 for 8 minutes and let them cool on cookie sheet for 4 minutes and they turned out to be so moist and chewy! I've always believed the longer things remain in the oven, the drier they seem to get, so I didn't want to bake them for 18-20 minutes at a lower temp. I made mine a little thicker and added a full tablespoon of cinnamon to the sugar/butter mixture and used half a tablespoon of cinnamon for the coating. They turned out absolutely delicious! New favourite!

I DO recommend doing the 300-degree oven; temp your oven—mine runs too hot. I used these to make sandwich cookies and they were perfect for that. First batch I accidentally did 350 & they got too crispy. Dough balls weighing .7 oz each baked 18 minutes at 300, rotated the baking sheet midway through. Silicone mats topped with parchment (because my old sheet pans are too dark). Rested on the sheet pan maybe 5 minutes, then slid the entire parchment sheet of cookies onto a cooling rack. Yielded an excellent chewy texture. 
The filling was cream cheese, salted butter, dulce de leche, powdered sugar & fine kosher salt.

Excellent. Everyone really loved them. Cinnamon subtle but nice.we used icing sugar with the cinnamon. Chilled the dough and had extra flour for the hands ready when we rolled the dough. Used the tip of 350 (325 on convection) for 9 minutes (had all for trays in at once) then on the cooling rack for 4 minutes.

I was looking for a strong cinnamon flavour, so I added 1.5 tsp each of cinnamon and nutmeg, as well as rolling the cookies in cinnamon-sugar. Following other reviewers' suggestions, I chilled the dough for half an hour and baked the cookies at 190°C for 13 minutes. They came out beautifully, not at all greasy as some people have found. My family loved them, I'm definitely making these again!

3.2.21 ... https://www.allrecipes.com/recipe/11310/cinnamon-sugar-butter-cookies-ii/ ... I'm a bit torn. These cookies are good, but man-oh-man did they spread & I chilled the dough. They spread to twice-plus the diameter of the uncooked dough. Adding a third to a half cup additional flour would help, yes; but I think the problem with this recipe is the temperature. The dough melted then cooked. Twenty minutes for a cookie is a long time. Addt'l flour, refrigerate & bake at 375/400. Three dozen cookies.

I'm quite sure I fallowed the recipe to a T. But they came out flat and greasy! Next time I would use more flour and chill the doug before baking. Maybe that would help? Had high hopes for these, turned out to be a bummer.

I tinkered with the recipe a llittle but the results sure panned out for it. I wanted a cinnamon cookie with bold cinnamon flavor so I added a teaspoon of cinnamon to the batter as well as a 10 oz. bag (1-2/3 cup) of cinnamon chips. I don't like flat cookies so I made sure to chill the dough well. Finally, I was not comfortable baking these at such a low oven temperature so I baked them at the more conventional temperature of 375 degrees for 8-9 minutes. They spread out to just the right thickness, neither too flat nor too thin. What did surprise me is how petite they turned out to be, only about 2 inches around. They're buttery, cinnamon-y, soft, yet chewy. Mom and Hubs were eating these before they even cooled and immediately proclaimed them a winner.
I added a bit more cinnamon, but the rest was the same. My son and I like them, and I'm sure my wife will love it. Great recipe that I'll make again.
Delicious! Made for a friend to cheer her up and she loved them! Family tried one and also loved. Super sticky dough, I would recommend refrigerating for like 20 minutes before rolling in sugar.
Made exactly as said. Husband said I could make anytime!!
I thought 18 minutes was too long. I was wrong.
I followed the recipe to the letter except like others, I refrigerated the dough for 20 mins before baking.
I followed the other note below and baked for 10 minutes at 375, they were perfect. Very close to a snickerdoodle.
Delicious simple cookies. Dipped in sugar mixture without refrigerating the dough. Rolled into balls nicely. Great to fill the cookie jar and freeze the rest.
not worth the effort
I Love the cinnaminny flavor. Great recipe
